name: Nifedipine
summary: A potent arterial vasodilator of the dihydropyridine class, used as an extended-release formulation for hypertension, stable and vasospastic angina, and Raynaud phenomenon.
mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing arteriolar dilation, reduced peripheral resistance, and lower afterload.

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Immediate release ~2 h; extended release ~7 h

dosing.adult: Hypertension/angina: extended-release 30–60 mg once daily, titrated as needed

safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk (small amounts); caution
warnings: Immediate-release capsules cause rapid vasodilation with reflex tachycardia — avoid for chronic hypertension
Peripheral edema is dose-related and often reflects arteriolar dilation, not fluid overload
Hypotension when combined with other antihypertensives
Grapefruit juice and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise exposure
safety.overdose: Hypotension with reflex tachycardia; treat with fluids and vasopressors.

clinicalPearls: Edema is the signature side effect — it is arteriolar dilation, so diuretics help less than expected.
Extended-release formulations are mandatory for chronic therapy; the sublingual/capsule use for hypertensive emergencies is obsolete.
good: Hypertension or vasospastic angina where pure arterial vasodilation is the goal.
bad: Severe aortic stenosis, HFrEF, or patients already troubled by edema.
